column1: text

AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC. It comes as the AI firm's boss has called for the technology's development to be slowed down, citing "serious" risks.
Iran war reshapes Brics ties but also exposes divisions. Brics members agree they need a new global order but it's harder to answer what should replace it and how to get there.
Six dead, 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes in Java Sea. Ships and helicopters are searching for those missing from the Virgo Transport 8 ship, which had encountered bad weather.

Turkish police detain dozens in raids on gay bars and homes of LGBTQ+ activists. Human rights groups in Turkey have accused the government of using a family- values campaign to target the LGBTQ+ community.
Trump doubles down on united Ireland comments on day two of visit. The US president was speaking at the Irish Open on Sunday and said "many people agree" with his comments.

They lost their jobs after posting about Charlie Kirk, but some have no regrets. Some people fired in the wake of Kirk's assassination have won big settlements from employers, others have had to start over from scratch.
Legendary Canadian boxer George Chuvalo dies aged 89. The heavyweight champion took on the likes of Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier, and was known for never once getting knocked out or knocked down.

US congressman swims to safety after his plane is forced to land on a lake. The small plane carrying Rep Tom Tiffany had a mechanical issue that forced the pilot to make an emergency landing on a Wisconsin lake.
Trump's comments on a united Ireland may have targeted audience across the Atlantic. Nobody could have predicted that today's main global headline would be Trump's desire to see a unified Ireland.

Only Roland Garros towel left, says Ukraine tennis player after Russian strike hits flat. Dayana Yastremska says her flat took a "direct hit" by a Russian missile in Odesa, and all that left was her Roland Garros towel.
Afghan woman deported from US in first use of 'alien terrorist' court. The legal US resident was never charged with a crime, but was deported due to her family links to terrorism.
Fire at nursing home in Chile kills 16 residents. Ten people were evacuated from the home in Araucanía region in central Chile.
Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down. The call comes amid growing concerns that AI models may become able to inflict serious damage worldwide.

Russians seek answers over hundreds missing after Ukraine's 2024 incursion. Officials say more than 300 Russians remain missing after the 2024 Kursk offensive, but no-one really knows the true figure.
Dramatic insider warnings over AI fall flat with some in Silicon Valley. A recent spate of stark warnings about the dangers of AI has been met with scepticism by executives and investors.

Critics celebrate Céline Dion's 'high-stakes' comeback show in Paris. The iconic Canadian singer kicked off her long-awaited comeback show in Paris on Saturday, after a six-year hiatus due to health issues.
Best friends for decades - until a DNA test revealed they were sisters. Meena Geltink and Minal Tijssen were adopted from orphanages in Mumbai in the 1980s and grew up in the Netherlands.
Céline Dion fans prepare for comeback concert in Paris. Fans of the Canadian singer greeted her as she left her hotel on Saturday.
How global trade and oil prices could be hit by Houthi advance. Yemen's Houthis have seized territory near the Bab al-Mandab Strait - a key trade gateway for oil and global shipping.

Has Trump won over voters with his midterm convention?. The BBC's North America editor Sarah Smith breaks down the main takeaways from the first-ever Republican convention held in the middle of a US presidential term.
Watch: Americans remember what they were doing on 9/11. The BBC asks people in Washington what they were doing on that day and how 11 September 2001 changed the country.

Brother of Muslim police cadet killed in 9/11 'disappointed' by calls for Mamdani to sit out memorial. Zeshan Hamdani speaks out after push back against New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who is Muslim, attending 9/11 events.
Drone display recreates the Twin Towers over New York City. Organisers say each of the 2,977 drones in the display represents a victim of the 9/11 attacks.

Reform confident it won't need to repay any of £72m under proposed new donor rules. Housing Secretary Angela Rayner says rule changes on donations from UK expats would apply retrospectively and anyone not complying with them would have "to return that money".
Andy Burnham among Great North Run finishers. This year's event sees 63,000 people take on the half marathon - including the prime minister.
'Slim chance' government will hit 1.5m new homes target, Rayner tells BBC. High construction costs and the Iran war are threatening the key manifesto pledge, the housing secretary says.

US embassy child abuse images suspect flown from UK before police interview. The individual worked at the US embassy in Vauxhall, south London, had diplomatic protection, despite not being a diplomat.
Tom Felton: I'm so excited to see Rupert Grint play Ron Weasley again. The Harry Potter actor talks about taking on Broadway and his friendship with former co-stars

Europe must endure winter of hardship to keep pressure on Putin, says PM's security adviser. In rare public remarks, Jonathan Powell said now was not the time for European nations to take their "foot off the gas".
Student loan terms to be made clearer in England following repayment row. Changes will spell out that governments can change rules and that career choices affect repayments.
Man charged with concealing identity at protest. Anti-migrant demonstrators marched in Portsmouth on Saturday, and a counter-protest was also held.
Flattened molars and facial pain: Why are more young people grinding their teeth?. Millions of us do it, though few of us realise we do - but getting the right treatment can be life-changing.
Diljit Dosanjh makes history under the famous Wembley arch. Wembley Stadium billed Diljit Dosanjh as the first Punjabi singer to headline the iconic music venue.
Will the Thirlwall report change the debate about Lucy Letby?. The inquiry into the former nurse is expected to find failures by her hospital to ensure patient safety.
In pictures: Thousands flock to Radio 2 in the Park in Stirling. The event, featuring a host of bands, singers and Radio 2 DJs is taking place at the foot of Stirling Castle.
Drag Race co-creator warns of TV representation 'crisis' after BBC drops show. The BBC is cutting the show because of financial pressures, sparking discussion about LGBTQ+ representation on TV.
Five night sky events to look out for this autumn. From meteor showers to a November supermoon, there are a number of impressive sights to behold in the autumn night sky.
Major fire at derelict mill featured in Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey. The mill, where Peaky Blinders was filmed, is already derelict after large fire in 2022.
BBC News app. Top stories, breaking news, live reporting, and follow news topics that match your interests
Will Reform Have To Give Their Mega Donations Back?. The government is trying to change the law but will it affect Reform’s record donations?
Americast. Trump made the pledge at the Republicans’ first ever midterm convention.
Star-studded, iconic, Oscar-winning mafia epic. Directed by Francis Ford Coppola and starring Al Pacino, Marlon Brando and Diane Keaton

Antonelli wins as Norris loses out under virtual safety car. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli wins the Spanish Grand Prix after McLaren's Lando Norris loses out because of the bad timing of a virtual safety car.

Garcia reality check bursts Benn's bubble in Vegas. As the biggest night of Conor Benn's career plummets into freefall in Las Vegas, what did we learn and what does it mean for the rest of his career?
Man charged following armed bus hijacking. The charges include kidnapping, hijacking, aggravated vehicle taking causing injury and possession of an offensive weapon.
Garcia crushes overmatched Benn in two rounds. Ryan Garcia crushed Briton Conor Benn with a ruthless second-round stoppage to retain his WBC welterweight crown in a world title mismatch in Las Vegas.
Shocked walker finds SUV blocking route on Wales Coast Path. It was jammed between a concrete fence post and a bench, and had been abandoned by the driver.

Watch: Is the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition worth the hype?. Crowds have been flocking to the British Museum to see the Bayeux Tapestry as it's on public display in the UK for the first time since it was created nearly 1,000 years ago.
Gruffalo Granny illustrator says rise of AI images 'worrying'. Axel Scheffler speaks to the BBC alongside author Dame Julia Donaldson, who reads an extract from their new book.
E-bike crime crackdown leads to 187 arrests. Footage released by the Met shows officers using high-powered Sur-Ron bikes to pursue suspects.
'Forget Notting Hill - we set our new romcom in the east end of Glasgow'. Romantic comedy Premature is out in cinemas next Friday, despite a microscopic budget.
Police probe use of firearm after man found dead in Armadale. Police were called to Harestanes Road at about 11:50 on Saturday where a 35-year-old man was pronounced dead.
Planned Gibraltar-sized rail testing centre has cost taxpayers £70m but hasn't been built. The site has not found private-sector funding because the risk is "too great," its boss says.
US prices remain high as fuel costs squeeze household budgets. Prices in the US rose 3.4% in the 12 months to August,  according to the latest official report on inflation.
Ryanair boss O'Leary defends 'high-fare rapists' airlines remarks. O'Leary has said airline passengers "can't afford to fly with the high-fare rapists around Europe".

'Skimpflation' warning as tinned mackerel alternative hits more supermarket shelves. Consumer group Which? has called the sale of jack mackerel, a cheaper, less nutritious species of fish, an example of "skimpflation".
Interest rates could rise again across the world – here's why. As countries grapple with energy costs pushing up inflation, this month will see how central banks respond.
AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July. The economy expanded by 0.4%, official figures show, whereas analysts had predicted no growth.
Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet. The government says the work will support thousands of jobs across the UK.
Air traffic chaos and compensation: 'Shutdown cost us more than £1,000'. Flight disruption has ruined holidays and left passengers sleeping on airport floors - so what are their rights?
Primark finally set to launch home deliveries. The retailer launches the service four years after making its first foray into internet shopping.
The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses. What makes someone stand out in a crowded workplace? Six business leaders tell us what they look for.
Oil, gas and borrowing costs surge as fears over Middle East escalate. The price of oil jumps to $105 a barrel amid signs the Iran war will not be resolved quickly.
Apple's new boss starts with big gamble on £1,999 first folding iPhone. Apple showed off at an event the first major design change to the iPhone in almost 20 years.
Labour mayors in England vow to cap tourist tax at 5%. Reform UK and the Conservatives have criticised plans for the new levy on visitors' overnight stays.
Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary. Heidi Alexander orders an investigation into the glitch that caused more than 2,000 flight cancellations.
Tax banks to cut energy bills, unions tell Burnham. The TUC says a bank surcharge should be reversed - and estimates it would raise £9bn over four years.
What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed?. Flights are cancelled owing to air traffic control problems, so what are your rights if you're affected?
Learner drivers still forced to wait months for tests. The Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency had been given a target to reduce average wait times to seven weeks.
Petrol prices rise by 5p over a week as Iran war sends oil higher. A litre of unleaded now costs 167.17p which is the biggest weekly increase since April, data shows.
Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans'. It is the latest in a series of increasing warnings about the safety threat posed by artificial intelligence.
I'm 27 and I've already written my will - here's why. For many young people making a will may not seem necessary, but here's why you shouldn't put it off.
Cowboy builder tore my home apart and disappeared off the face of the Earth with £14k. Victims of cowboy builders describe how they were exploited with one couple left "scarred for life".
Singaporean man pleads guilty in US to massive crypto heist. Malone Lam and his associates used the proceeds of their crimes to fund a luxurious lifestyle, US authorities said.
OpenAI says it cracked 90-year-old maths problem in 88 hours. OpenAI's claim that it solved parts of Navier-Stokes equations has quickly stirred controversy.
More flight cancellations as fallout from air traffic control glitch continues. Departures from a number of airports are affected by a technical problem affecting air traffic control provider Nats.
US to ban imports of some Canadian alcohol, dairy goods and motorbikes. It is the latest strike in a long trade war, and comes after Canadian counter-tariffs on US goods come into force.
Can Europe recharge its battery industry?. Europe has some promising battery tech, but can it make up ground lost to Chinese battery giants?
I asked my husband to pay into my pension when we had a child - here's why. Molly and Taylor Haylett explain the changes to how they managed their finances when they started a family.
Why some experts increasingly fear AI will take over. AI agents went on an uncontrolled hacking spree, leaving some in the industry worried
Should promotion depend on how workers use AI?. More companies are tying career progression to AI use: is that fair?
'Tirana teeth': Albania hopes to be the new Turkey for dental work. The Balkan nation is aiming to become a new centre for medical tourism.
From 'dog fruit' to darling: India's avocado boom. Demand for avocados is booming in India and local growers hope to grab more of the market.
Prosecco, cakes and beauty products - how to get birthday freebies and why there's a catch. Cake, coffee, make-up and burgers are just some of the free things you can get on your birthday.
Why wait? Business grads buying firms to install themselves as CEO. Impatient to be the boss of an established company they are borrowing money to fund their purchases.

'My parents won't lend me £10k but helped my brother': When families play financial favourites. So-called financial favouritism can cause jealousy and resentment long into adulthood. Here is how experts say you can avoid it
Overcooked? Why robotic pizza makers are failing. A string of failures has sapped confidence that robots will take over production at pizza restaurants.
How Dolly Parton's business savvy helped her succeed far beyond the charts. While country music and films brought her fame, her entrepreneurial zeal brought her fortune.
Firms scramble for battery power in Spain and Portugal. After last year's massive power failure Spanish and Portuguese firms are buying battery back ups.
'What you see is what you pay' - why some US restaurants are banning tips. Tips are central to US dining culture but some eateries think that they are unfair.
Drought leaves 'barely any apples' to make cider. Some orchards are harvesting just a 10th of their usual crop, and facing an uncertain future.
How landscape gardening is being electrified. The switch to quieter electric equipment is not going as fast as some would like.
'It's cost upon cost for working families - they get no help'. The government needs to do more to support working families, a charity in Rotherham says.
Oil prices create 'huge worry' as winter looms. The warning comes after the US-Iran conflict drives up heating oil and fuel costs.
Ending rough sleeping is 'not just a housing issue'. Andy Burnham wants to get people "in from the cold" by Christmas, but the scale of the task is huge.
Can you really juggle a job and study for a degree?. Students in Glasgow say the cost of living is making part-time work increasingly important.

Aviation faces hotter, stormier skies – and passengers might have to accept more disruption. Are people going to have to increasingly accept more delays and diversions as the effects of climate change intensify?
Why the UK is dithering over what to do about e-scooters. Why is it taking so long for the government to regulate them, and what are the consequences of delay?
Why Gen Z are planning for life without a state pension. Many younger people do not believe the state pension will exist when they are older
The furious dispute over what caused Air India flight 171 to crash. The final conclusions of the investigation have yet to be published, although more could become apparent in the coming days.
How the High Street became a window on our political instability. High Streets have declined in recent years. What does this tell us about the UK?

Watch: Three times Trump has promised money to Americans. The BBC's Samira Hussain looks at the president's past claims after he announced he would pay American adults $5,000 if Republicans win in the midterm elections.
When a Dragon gives you a helping hand. When a Dragon gives you a helping hand
Primark introduces home delivery. Primark has said it plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain, four years after it made its first foray into e-commerce.
Why a famous Montreal sandwich shop has been forced to swap its soda. Schwartz’s, one of Montreal’s most famous delis, has changed suppliers for its black cherry soda.
How much can Canada fight back in its trade war with the US?. The US may be the bigger trading partner, but Canada shouldn't be counted out quite yet in the escalating trade fight.
PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?. The BBC's Tom Gerken plays the hotly anticipated superhero game from Spider-Man makers Insomniac.
UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI. The Cabinet Office, which leads on AI safety, says the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".
Does this AI comic make you laugh?. Comedian Garrett Millerick has created an AI avatar based on his own material. Is it any good?

Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons. The revelations in Anthropic's threat intelligence report come after a former top researcher at the company warned of the risks of AI to humanity.
UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog. The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon tells the BBC.
Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe. The US tech giant says the €13bn data centre project will create tens of thousands of jobs.
White House pulls Tetris-style 'Build The Wall' game after copyright concern. The Tetris Company says it takes "copyright infringement very seriously" and is not involved with the game.
Meta continues to run ads promoting child sexual abuse material in India - report. The report follows a BBC Eye investigation that found Instagram running paid ads promoting such material in India.
Tech Life. Scammers demand money from Instagram users over fake copyright claims.
Tech Now. Shiona McCallum meets mums and hospital staff trialling a new assisted birth innovation.
Summer wildfires caused catastrophic hidden damage, scientists warn. Bangor University researchers say the scale of damage is far greater than what is immediately visible.
Record heatwaves in France set to make champagne stronger. Winemakers can produce bubbly up to 15% ABV following an unusual harvest that produced sweeter grapes.
Battle to save the tiny, gooey snail only found in one lake in the UK. Once prevalent across the UK, this mollusc is now only found in one lake in Wales.
Sheen says he was snubbed by FM over pollution claims. The actor urged MPs to back a national testing programme to make sure historic toxic dump sites were safe.
El Niño likely to cause wetter and warmer-than-normal autumn. A warmer and wetter-than-normal autumn is in store for the UK, according to the latest Met Office forecasts.
Species 'at risk of vanishing' from area of Wales' largest national park. The National Trust warns species are on the brink of extinction in a valley of Eryri - Snowdonia - National Park.

New hurricane season record as 'historic' El Niño leaves Atlantic eerily quiet. The Atlantic hurricane season has reached its climatological peak, but a strong El Niño means no hurricanes have formed this year.
August joint hottest month on record globally. BBC Weather Presenter Simon King explains the figures.
August joint-hottest month on record as climate change and El Niño drive heat. Climate change and the rising influence of El Niño saw August reach the record for warmest month.

Watch: Downed trees and flooding as Hurricane Lowell batters western Hawaii. The storm brought damaging winds and torrential rain to parts of the island on Monday and Tuesday, triggering concerns about flash flooding and mudslides.
How cleaning up the air is speeding up global warming - and revealing a bigger problem. A curious online row over this summer's heatwaves points to a wider - and worrying - shift in climate science.
Gaps in evidence on vaccinating badgers against TB, researchers say. Researchers want increased monitoring of the vaccination's impact on the disease and a review of the evidence.
Residents and officials meet on dredging concerns. Officers plan to meet with a complainant in the coming days over the dredging at St Aubin's  Bay.
The slow, muddy work of saving ancient bogs. Sarah Hickey and her team help keep nearly 20,000 acres of upland in the Isle of Man healthy.
Town gets in a flap over High Street pigeon mess. Some people say the pigeons are a pest, while others think the birds are being unfairly demonised.
Shetland spaceport project secures £30m of UK government investment. The funding will be used to build two more launchpads.
Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty. The Isle of Man Mars Society is urging politicians to sign an international space exploration agreement.
How a new instrument could reveal the secrets of the stars. MOONS, which was built by a team lead from Scotland, has started its work at the Very Large Telescope in Chile.
Scientists may have found first hint of dark matter. The mysterious material has eluded scientists for nearly a century.
BBC Inside Science. Prof Stuart Russell offers some advice following a report into July’s Hugging Face hack.
First dinosaur bone from Antarctica found in a drawer. The fossil, collected in Antarctica in 1985, is part of the tail of a beast called a Titanosaur.
Fossil identified as first dinosaur ever found in Antarctica. Argentinian geologist Eduardo Olivero became the first scientist to find the remains of a dinosaur in Antarctica in 1986.
Simpler, older version of Stonehenge found three miles from famous site. The structure consisted of two posts that lined up with the solstices 5,000 years ago.
From blast off to splashdown: My days following Nasa's historic mission to the Moon. BBC Science Editor Rebecca Morelle reflects on how it felt to watch history being made.

The 40 minutes when the Artemis crew loses contact with the Earth. As the astronauts pass behind the Moon they will experience a moment of silence and solitude as communication with the Earth is blocked.
How the UK's extreme heat is shifting the conversation about air-con. Should we embrace air conditioning despite its costs and consequences?
The hidden cost of the night shift and how to sleep it off. More than three million people in the UK work night shifts, which can greatly impact their health. What can be done to help them?

After record heat, could the Atlantic make Britain's weather even more extreme?. As temperatures rise, scientists are investigating whether a changing Atlantic could bring more volatile weather to the UK
Why cheap power could matter more than clean power in the push for net zero. The question of how important making our electricity clean is to going green is coming under increasing scrutiny
Some dentists say more young people are grinding their teeth - are you one of them?. Millions of us do it, though few of us realise we do - but getting the right treatment can be life-changing.
Running costs of vaccine damage scheme more than double amount paid to victims. The cost of administration and medical checks has now topped £83m, according to new figures.
Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world. About 400 million people have access to some form of assisted dying - what are the policies of other countries?

'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times. Cancer care has got worse since the government announced plans to speed up waiting times and save more lives, BBC analysis shows.
Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat. Pharmacies in England will soon offer treatments for a total of 12 common conditions which save people going to their GP first.
Very hot drinks may damage the food pipe and increase cancer risk. Steaming hot liquid can damage the cell lining on the way down to the stomach, experts say.
Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds. About 7% of those polled wanted disability benefit cuts, according to the latest British Social Attitudes survey.
Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital. One parent says the number of patients involved in a review is "ridiculous".
A&E did not get the basics right - my son's life was ruined at 32. Oli's experience is one of a growing number of clinical negligence claims being made in England, BBC analysis shows.
BBC News presenter reveals she has blood cancer. Maryam Moshiri tells the BBC she wanted to reveal her diagnosis to raise awareness about the cancer.
How hunger for a new weight-loss drug is feeding an industry of fakes. Dupes of retatrutide are flooding the black market, but the drug is yet to be approved by regulators.
'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health. Sleeping next to a snorer could be having a negative effect on your health, experts tell the BBC.
Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts. Menstrual cycles are highly individual, making blanket advice found on social media difficult to apply, researchers say.
Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse. The things you're doing to make your sleep better could actually be making your sleep worse.

Off to Reading or Leeds? Here's your guide to festival make-up (without the toxins). Neon is on trend, but some make-up products pose a serious risk to your health. Here's what to check for, and how to dazzle.
What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?. Men who have had the procedure can expect 10-20% more girth for the next six to nine months - but it can go wrong.
Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England. It follows the UK's largest and fastest growing meningitis B outbreak to date in Kent earlier this year.
What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?. Some people can carry bacteria in their nose or throat without getting sick, but can spread it to others.
More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave. When turning on the oven is a no-no and you're bored of salads, these foods (and drinks) will help to beat the heat.
What does hot weather do to the body?. Hot weather during the summer can affect anyone, but some people run a greater risk of serious harm.
What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?. Some UV exposure is essential for our wellbeing, but too much is damaging and can cause skin cancer.
Mums 'left to get on with it' after C-sections. Mothers have described being left to recover from caesarean sections with "no support".
New mums 'left to get on with it' as C-section numbers hit record high. Mothers have described being left to recover from caesarean sections with "no support".
Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain. Lhamo Weston says it's important to be open about competing with endometriosis
Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'. Lucy Shepherd is one of 90 women to take part in a trial helping cancer survivors come off medication.
Wellbeing walks praised for keeping people active. The free walks range from 10 to 90 minutes and are aimed at all abilities.
Train station to mark World Suicide Prevention Day. As well as offering advice, Wellbeing Week will include poetry, gardening workshops, art and music.
New GP and wellbeing hub 'a major milestone'. The £21m hub brings together primary care, community wellbeing and leisure services in one location.
'I'm on a mission to convince people to work less'. Jo Hooper spent her 20s chasing career success, but had two work-related breakdowns before she was 31.
New home means 'big ambitions' for wood enterprise. Wolverhampton Wood Recycling's bigger premises will bring more volunteers together, its founders say.
Covid inquiry PPE report - key findings. What went wrong with the government's planning and buying of vital items like gloves and gowns that cost taxpayers billions of pounds.

UK wasted £10bn on PPE that left NHS staff poorly protected, Covid inquiry finds. Healthcare staff were unable to properly protect themselves, or those in their care, from dangerous infections, says the latest inquiry report.
UK begins trials of Ebola vaccine developed in just eight weeks. The UK medicines regulator has given approval for an experimental vaccine to be tested on healthy adults.
'World-first' vaccine designed by artificial intelligence. Cambridge scientists say they have, for the first time, tested a vaccine designed by AI.
Doctors vote to take strike action in row over pay. The British Medical Association is in dispute with Manx Care over "pay erosion since 2008".

Resident doctors take strike action over pay. The BMA said there will "undoubtedly be cancellation of operations, outpatient appointments and elective care" but "patient safety will still be prioritised".
Consultants and specialist doctors take strike action over pay. Full emergency cover remained in place and patients were told to attend all scheduled appointments unless advised otherwise.
A&E to remain open as doctors' strike called off. Resident doctor strikes are now on pause while they consider a new pay offer form the government.
Resident doctors cancel strike after new offer from government. The walkout had been due to start at 07:00 BST on Monday and last until Friday.
Inside Health. Plus, how much do people really change their habits for a free coffee?
'Game-changing' suicide prevention charity expands. The charity provides safe spaces for men to talk about their emotions without being judged.

William and Catherine praise role of sports in suicide prevention. The Princess of Wales has made a surprise appearance alongside her husband the Prince of Wales, as he gave an impassioned call to the sports sector to help prevent suicides.

How can sport help mental health?. At the launch of On Your Side, a mental health toolkit created by the Prince of Wales and the Royal Foundation, BBC Sport's Nesta McGregor asks sporting stars, 'how has sport helped your mental health?'
Campaigners hold vigil as stroke unit closes. Patients needing urgent care will be taken to Taunton or Dorchester instead.
What in the World. More people are doing it to feel confident socialising - but what are the risks?

'She's back': Fans dance, sing and cry after Céline Dion's comeback concert in Paris. Thousands turned out to witness Céline Dion perform in Paris on Saturday, her first show after a six year illness-induced hiatus.
Watch: Fantasia on British Sea-Songs at the Last Night of the Proms. Sir Henry Wood composed the melody for the centenary of the Battle of Trafalgar in 1905.

Oscar-winning film producer Jeremy Thomas dies aged 77. Best known for The Last Emperor and Sexy Beast, the British film-maker was celebrated for working with international directors throughout his decades-long career.

Grammy-winning US rapper Lil Durk acquitted in murder-for-hire trial. The Chicago rapper was arrested in 2024 and accused of involvement in a shooting that killed the cousin of rival rapper Quando Rondo.
We've followed their lives for six decades - now the stars of 7 Up are bowing out. 70 Up is the final instalment in a series which began in 1964 and has followed the lives of 14 people.
Five minutes to steal a Renoir: Why museum thefts are becoming bolder across Europe. Art crime investigators and security experts say burglaries from galleries across Europe are becoming more brazen.
The Prodigy to headline Creamfields 2027. The dance music festival Creamfields has announced The Prodigy as its first headline act.
Life after Eurovision for Look Mum No Computer. The musician behind Eins, Zwei, Drei says people still stop him in the street after Eurovision.
Noel Gallagher says Johnny Marr has 'always been gung-ho' with his guitars. The band borrowed one of Marr's instruments which was used on the cover of Oasis' 1994 debut single Supersonic.
How a BBC strike exterminated Doctor Who adventure. Marcus Hearn recalls the stories his father told him about the filming of episodes in Cambridge.
Stacey Solomon and Alesha Dixon to host The Voice UK in ITV revamp. The pair replace Emma Willis, who has hosted the show since 2014 but is leaving to front Strictly.
Oasis tease tour announcement with drone display. The band illuminated the sky over the Etihad's Joie Stadium, home to Manchester City Woman.

Céline Dion duets with fan ahead of Paris comeback concert. The Canadian singer - who was diagnosed with an incurable condition four years ago - has been interacting with fans outside her hotel, ahead of a much-anticipated show on Saturday.
Museum agrees to return remains to ancestral homeland. Oxford's Pitt Rivers Museum will return more than three dozen sets of human remains to the Naga people.
James Bay performs with broken ankle at Bon Jovi gig. The Hitchin-born star is wheeled onto the stage with his leg in a cast for his set at Wembley.
Bids encouraged to keep famed artwork in the UK. Sir Stanley Spencer is synonymous with Cookham, where he was born, lived and set some of his work.
Farmer left in abandoned, freezing town without food and water for TV show. Ioan Humphreys said he had "zero idea" about what he was getting into in the survival show.
Bayeux Tapestry unveiled to UK public for first time at British Museum. Visitors tell the BBC it was a "real privilege" to be among the first to see the tapestry in England.
People long for simpler times, say Practical Magic reboot stars. Actresses Maisie Williams and Joey King feature in the upcoming sequel of the 1998 fantasy romcom.
New Strictly hosts explain their roles as they reject 'roving presenter' reports. Johannes Radebe, Josh Widdicombe and Emma Willis say their roles are not "fixed" or defined.
Alan Carr holds back tears on special night at National Television Awards. The comedian and Celebrity Traitors win big - see a full list of winners and nominees from the 26th edition of the awards.

When the ground is thoroughly wet, after excess rainwater has run off it is said to be at field capacity. Meteorologists describe drought in terms of soil moisture deficit (SMD) from field capacity.
